title: Quantified availability & latency targets with progressive-release guardrails for Inference API
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Background: As Redwood grows enterprise usage for Redwood API, customers require explicit, testable behavior guarantees for production inference. Existing doc fragments list SLOs and rollout gates in separate places; this ticket consolidates quantified targets (p50/p95/p99 latency, availability SLOs, error budget) and ties them to progressive-release guardrails (canary thresholds, automatic rollback triggers, cross-region fallback).

Objective: Produce a concise PRD and acceptance criteria that define: 1) per-route latency targets for typical inference workloads (chat/generation/embeddings), 2) availability and error-budget definitions expressed as objective metrics and alerting thresholds, and 3) an explicit progressive-release gating matrix mapping metric breaches to rollout actions (pause, rollback, increase canary traffic, require manual approval).

Out of scope: Per-model micro-SLOs for third-party model variants, long-term latency tuning experiments (those belong to ENG runway tickets), and commercial SLA contract language (legal will adapt outputs from this PRD).

Stakeholders: PM (Sofia Ramirez), Eng Reliability (Liam O'Connor), Runtime Lead (Nina Chen), Observability (Marcus Li), Customer Success (Priya Nair), Security & Compliance (Amina Yusuf).
acceptance_criteria: A PRD doc (single page + appendix) created and reviewed by stakeholders that lists concrete numeric targets for p50/p95/p99 latency and availability/uptime per product surface (hosted API, dedicated, private)
An error-budget definition and burn rate policy with automation hooks: when burn rate > 2x for 1h -> page on-call; if >4x for 3h -> initiate rollback and throttle canaries
A progressive-release gate matrix that maps metric thresholds to actions and is machine-actionable (i.e., can be wired into Console rollout engine or runbook automation)
Unit-testable alert thresholds and dashboard panels scoped in Observability (links to dashboards included) and validated on synthetic traffic
Approval from Reliability and Observability teams on the thresholds and rollback actions documented in the PRD
Acceptance includes example rollout scenarios (slowdown, error spike, regional outage) with documented runbook steps and expected system behavior
decisions: Adopt quantiles p50/p95/p99 for latency reporting and use p95 as primary rollout gating signal for canaries
Define availability SLO as 99.95% monthly for hosted API (P1 customers) and 99.9% for dedicated; private deployments documented as 'customer-managed' with recommended targets
Error budget window: rolling 30-day window. Automatic rollback if error-rate spend exceeds 40% of budget within 24 hours and absolute error-rate > 0.5%
Canary progression: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 4 hours default with health checks at each step; adjustable per-release via rollout config
tradeoffs: Stricter latency gates reduce release velocity for high-impact runtime changes but improve customer experience; chosen thresholds aim for conservative safety while allowing emergency fast paths
Using p95 as the gate balances sensitivity to regressions and noise; p99 would be too noisy for small canary sizes
Rolling 30-day error budget gives long-term stability signal but may mask short bursty incidents; mitigated by burn-rate policies for short-term spikes
